header.intro: Send a value across the boundary between parent and child. Then follow the reply returning as an event and see the code involved in each passage.
header.imageAlt: Māyā, Kalika, and Bhu study a book among lanterns and luminous Angular component diagrams.

exhibit.title: Parent, child, and the path back
exhibit.intro: The parent holds the message and Angular carries it to the child. The child chooses a reply and emits a return event. You trigger the flow; the interface records each passage.

guide.title: Send the message through the circuit

parent.title: The parent sends
parent.text: Write a message or use the example.

child.title: The child chooses
child.text: Read the received value and select a reply.

return.title: The parent receives
return.text: Watch the event return with the selected reply.

parent.title: The sender
parent.label: Message for the child component
parent.hint: Not sure what to write? Start with a ready-made message.
parent.inputNote: is a property binding: it carries the value from the parent to the child's input.

child.title: The receiver
child.waiting: The child is still waiting for a value from the parent.
child.reply: Choose a reply from the child
child.outputNote: creates an output through which the child emits an event to its container.

responses.acknowledge: Child: message received. The complete value arrived.
responses.measure: Child: I processed the value. It contains {{ count }} characters.

timeline.title: What happened beneath the interface
timeline.note: This panel does not receive clicks. It only records, in order, what your actions trigger in the circuit above.
timeline.parentState: The parent updates the value stored in its state.
timeline.binding: Angular evaluates the expression bound to the message property.
timeline.childInput: The child receives the new value through its @Input.
timeline.childOutput: When clicked, the child emits an event through @Output.
timeline.parentHandler: The parent handles the event and updates its interface again.

parent.title: 1. The parent prepares and sends the value
parent.description: Signals hold the message while the send method updates the value that will be delivered to the child.

binding.title: 2. The template creates the connection
binding.description: Property binding sends the value through [message]. Event binding listens for the reply through (reply).

child.title: 3. The child receives and prepares a reply
child.description: @Input creates the child's entry point. @Output and EventEmitter create the path back to the parent component.

return.title: 4. The parent handles the reply
return.description: The method receives the object emitted by the child, stores the reply in a Signal, and advances the visual log.

action.title: What do you do?
action.text: Write a message, send it to the child, and ask it to reply. Each action changes the visible stage of the experiment.

angular.title: What does Angular notice?
angular.text: It detects the change, reevaluates the connection between components, and updates only the interface fragments that depend on those values.

code.title: What moves in the code?
code.text: The value moves down from parent to child through @Input. The event returns from child to parent through @Output and EventEmitter.

header.intro: Choose a subject and open a passage to a real collection. The interface turns the waiting period, the response, and even the failure of a REST request into something you can follow.
header.imageAlt: Māyā contemplates her maned-wolf form as they float among luminous orbits and a cosmic cube.

exhibit.title: Invoke an image of the cosmos
exhibit.intro: Your action creates an HTTP request to NASA's collection. The JSON provides metadata and an image address; the browser fetches that file in a second request to reveal the result inside the portal.

controls.label: Cosmic subject · search in English
controls.placeholder: E.g. Orion nebula, mars, black hole...

idle.title: The portal is at rest
idle.text: No request has been sent. Choose a subject to begin the crossing.

imageLoading.title: Revealing
imageLoading.text: Metadata arrived. Loading the image file.

empty.title: Nothing crossed
empty.text: The search for “{{ query }}” returned no record with a displayable image.

error.title: The passage was interrupted
error.text: The request failed before delivering a usable response. The error state is also part of the flow.

imageError.title: The image did not manifest
imageError.text: The data arrived, but the visual file could not be loaded.

announcement.loading: Request started. The portal is loading.
announcement.empty: The request finished without a displayable image.
announcement.error: The request finished with an error.

inspector.title: What crossed the portal
inspector.intro: This is not a simulation: these are the method, address, parameters, and mapped result from the real request.

action.title: 1. The action enters the stream
action.description: Submitting the form reads the current subject and publishes it into a Subject, which acts as the entry point to the asynchronous stream.

request.title: 2. The service builds the GET
request.description: HttpParams builds a text search (q) or targets a selected record (nasa_id). HttpClient sends the GET and returns an Observable of the typed HTTP response.

stream.title: 3. The Observable coordinates time
stream.description: switchMap abandons an earlier request when another one starts. catchError turns a failure into a state the interface can present.

mapping.title: 4. The DTO becomes a view model
mapping.description: The service reads collection.items and preserves the HTTPS preview URL. Selected examples also check nasa_id so a different record is not substituted. Receiving metadata does not mean the image has loaded: the browser still needs to fetch it.

action.title: What do you do?
action.text: Choose a subject and submit the form. That event is the request's starting point.

angular.title: What does Angular notice?
angular.text: State changes from idle to loading and then to success, empty, or error. Each change updates only the matching representation.

code.title: What moves in the code?
code.text: Text enters the RxJS stream, HttpClient receives JSON, and the service maps the external DTO into a small, safe model for the interface.
